KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a structurally excellent franchise with durable competitive advantages, but the stock is priced at the ceiling of its 12-month valuation range with no margin of safety. The P/E of 28.4x sits at the 97th percentile of its 12-month range, while the 3.5% earnings yield is 95bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%. The multiple re-expansion from 23x to 28x was driven by sentiment (VIX collapse from 31 to 16) rather than proven earnings acceleration—the quant data window only covers Q1-Q2 2025. While Q1 2026 results (10% organic growth, 18% EPS growth) partially justify the re-rating, the stock has already priced in this improvement. Rising rates (+40bp in 90 days) and oil (+30%) create headwinds for a high-multiple defensive. A reversion to the 12-month median P/E of ~25x implies ~12% downside. The IRS transfer-pricing dispute represents an unresolved multi-billion-dollar liability excluded from guidance. Near-term catalysts are absent—no earnings event, no capital-allocation shift, no regulatory clear. The risk/reward is asymmetric: limited upside at peak multiples, material downside if rates stay elevated or the multiple mean-reverts.
